newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stock draw, cold Europe lift gas oil barges.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock draw, cold Europe lift gas oil barges.

text.p: Cold weather in Europe and a surprise fall in U.S. distillate stocks lifted outright gas oil values and barge premiums Friday, traders said.
Freezing temperatures in northwest Europe and little sign of a change over the weekend were encouraging inland German demand but ARA barge markets were thin with many players still absent.
"It is cold here but there are few people to do business with," said a German barge trader.
Refinery heating oil for very prompt loading traded at $217.00 a tonne and at Jan IPE evens but premiums for first half Jan barrels talked firmer.
Sellers were asking Jan IPE +$1.25 a tonne in anticipation of renewed demand once the holiday period ends, traders said.
"Barges are moving up but we'll have to wait until people get back next week before we see things happening," said a trader.

Jan IPE gas oil put on $2.25 to $217.75 a tonne by 1230 GMT, pushed higher by an unexpected fall in U.S. distillate stocks last week of between 1.5-2.0 million barrels. U.S. traders had been expecting a build.
Cargo markets were extremely thin with premiums notionally unchanged. --Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
